summary: Claude loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and said the task was bounded. It asked one clarifying question, then laid out hard cut vs. word boundary in chat, recommended word boundary, and asked "Want me to build this?" before changing any code. After I approved, it edited format.js and format.test.js (red-then-green tests). It never wrote a spec file, and there is no docs/ directory in the repo.
reasoning: All seven criteria have evidence from the screen, the session log, or the filesystem. The agent said the task was bounded and presented both alternatives in chat with a recommendation. It waited for approval, with no repo changes before approval per git status and the log. It never wrote a spec (no docs/ directory exists), and it started implementing after I approved.

observations.description: Before the approach gate, the agent asked a second design question nobody raised: whether '...' counts toward maxLength. It used an AskUserQuestion picker. The question was reasonable, but it adds a round-trip on a bounded task. I picked the recommended option.

The brainstorming skill ran the Codex approach gate (codex-preflight, then codex-companion.mjs against the seeded stub) and wrote approach-context.md and approach-prompt.md under $HOME/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review. The stub returned '{}'. None of this was shown on screen, and the chat never said whether Codex reviewed the approach or what it returned.

On first launch, Claude Code's workspace trust dialog and the Bypass Permissions warning both had 'No, exit' selected by default. I had to press Down before Enter on each. This is harness/onboarding friction, not a product defect.

The agent flagged a problem in the fixture itself: format.test.js uses console.assert, which does not set a non-zero exit code, so the suite prints 'All tests passed' even when assertions fail. Node also warns that package.json lacks "type": "module".

criteria.evidence: The screen showed "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill". In the session log, the first tool_use is {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}}, and it comes before any Edit.

Screen: "Classifying first: this is bounded — format() already exists at format.js:2, and choosing between two truncation algorithms inside it names no new structure. So I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec."

criteria.criterion: Approach gate: both alternatives presented in chat and approval asked before code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "A — Hard cut. str.slice(0, max - 3) + '...'" / "B — Word boundary, hard-cut fallback" / "I recommend B." / "Want me to build this?" At that point, `git status --short` in the workdir printed nothing (no changes), and the log had no Edit calls yet. The two Edit calls came only after my approval message.

criteria.criterion: No spec file in docs/superpowers/specs or docs/hyperpowers/specs
criteria.evidence: `ls docs` → "ls: docs: No such file or directory". `git status --short` shows only " M format.js" and " M format.test.js". The only Write calls went to home/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review/.../approach-context.md and approach-prompt.md, which are Codex gate scratch files outside the repo. `find . ../home -path '*specs*'` (excluding plugins) returned nothing.
The only classification on screen was "this is bounded". The agent never mentioned a spike or a feasibility question.

criteria.criterion: Did not classify as architectural / write spec
criteria.evidence: The agent said it would "present a short design in chat rather than write a spec". No spec file exists (see criterion 4).

After "truncate at word boundary sounds better, go ahead with that", the log shows: Bash node format.test.js (baseline), Edit format.test.js, Bash (confirm the new tests fail), Edit format.js, Bash (run the full suite). Screen: "Done. All 14 assertions pass".
